about: Field Books 11 to 18 of 24: the eight found on hour two's ground (the black beach, the Sounding Ring, the Glass, the Malpaís, the Kiln Yards, the hornito field, the Scar). Lore only, in W1's shape: one ruled page in Plex Mono (lines already broken, at most 58 characters), a sketch for the page's corner, and the single mark it inks on the map. 'loading' is the one line the Loading screen may show. 'place' names where it lies (the items lane places it).

books.title: LOG OF THE PAN KITE
books.found: in the wreck's dry locker, above the tide line
page: Up at first light, 40 m on the line, wind 045.
The Glass clear to the Ring. Gauge on Sluice 3.
Noon: dust from the south, sudden. Brought her down
to 20 m and the line went slack under me.
She went into the surf off the beach and broke
both cells. I walked home with the bar in my hand.
Note for the guild: never keep one kite.
books.sketch: a box kite nosing into a breaking wave, its line looping slack, a small figure on the sand holding a bar
books.loading: Note for the guild: never keep one kite.

books.title: LEVEL BOOK 8 · THE RING
books.hand: a leveller of the Datum Survey
books.found: in a bronze tube bolted to the Ring's south flange
page: The Ring stands 34 m across and leans as built.
It is not a door. It is the bay's level.
The sounding balloon is moored to its foot
on one line. It reads the bay's depth by the
hour and the Gauge keeps the pans to it.
If the line is ever cut the balloon goes
downwind and keeps reading where it lands.
Do not cut the line.
books.sketch: the leaning ring in elevation, a moored balloon drawn small at its foot on a single dashed line

inks.what: Benchmark 3 at the foot of the Ring's rise

books.loading: It is not a door. It is the bay's level.

books.title: TALLY OF THE GLASS
books.hand: a salt-raker of the Pan Houses
books.found: wedged in the bronze post's cap in the Glass
page: The post in the Glass stands a metre proud.
My grandmother said it was put there to tell
the sea where it lives.
Three tides a month it reads high and the Gauge
walks out to it and stands. We lose a day's
rake each time. Nobody has asked the post why.
Raked 40 baskets on the dry days. 12 on the wet.
books.sketch: a bronze post standing in shallow water, a tide mark scratched on it, a basket beside it

inks.what: Benchmark 2, the post in the Glass

books.loading: It was put there to tell the sea where it lives.

books.title: SHIFT BOOK · NO. 2 WELL
books.hand: a well-keeper of the geothermal plant
books.found: in the pump house's rusted cabinet, behind the racks
page: Four wells on the bench, 10 m apart, all hot.
Brine tank full at the west end. Gauges steady.
Something new came up the road at noon:
a kiln on four legs with a hose. It coupled to
No. 2 like it had read the drawings.
Quenched No. 2 to see. It stood a while, cold,
then walked to No. 3. The other one watched.
Shift ends. Leave the tank full.
books.sketch: four wellheads in a row on a bench, a squat kiln on four legs coupled to the second by a hose

inks.what: the brine quench tank at the bench's west end

books.loading: It coupled to No. 2 like it had read the drawings.

books.title: WHAT THE TOWERS WERE
books.found: under a fallen tile at the foot of the tall tower
page: Two towers, 26 m and 22 now. Once higher.
Tiled white, steam out the top all day,
and power down the cables to the Datum's works.
My father's father took the bronze off
the racks to make our first forge. The Kilns
came for the heat after the works went dark.
They don't want us. They want the wells warm.
books.sketch: two broken cooling towers in profile, tiles fallen at their feet, a smith's hammer laid across the margin
books.loading: They don't want us. They want the wells warm.

books.title: LEVEL BOOK 15 · RUST CONE
books.hand: a leveller of the Datum Survey
books.found: in the pillar's step at the top of Rust Cone
page: T3 set on the cone's rim, 145 m. Red scree,
steep, and it slides under the tripod.
From here: T4 on the ridge, T1 far west over
the pans, the Ring's lean on the shore.
Below to the south the flow is still warm
in the night. Do not set benchmarks on it
for a year. It is still deciding its shape.
books.sketch: a cinder cone with a pillar on its rim and three bearing lines to tiny pillars, the scree hatched red
books.loading: It is still deciding its shape.

books.title: NOTES ON THE HORNITOS
books.found: in a crack of the third hornito, wrapped in felt
page: Seven chimneys of spatter, 3 to 6 m, each
standing on the roof of a lava tube.
The steam is the tube breathing out.
One tube is open at its mouth and dry inside.
A dead Peg nest at the back. Leave it be.
Wind down the Scar is straight and strong.
From the cone's lip a kite goes home in
one line, seven posts, if you keep to them.
books.sketch: a row of hornitos in section over a single tube, the tube's mouth open, a kite drawn tiny above
books.loading: The steam is the tube breathing out.

books.title: KITE LINES, THE SCAR
books.found: tied to the Scar's third line-post, in an oiled bag
page: The Scar runs 225, straight down the wind.
No ridge to ride. You glide it, that's all.
I set 7 posts on its north lip, 480 m end
to end. Keep the posts on your right hand
and you will land on the Scar's foot.
Lose height early and you walk the rest.
Last one I'll set down here. Knees.
books.sketch: the Scar as a straight band, seven small posts along its upper edge, a kite's track beside them

inks.what: the first post on the Scar's north lip

books.loading: No ridge to ride. You glide it, that's all.
